[[Sporting News|SN]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] ([[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013]]) * First-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2014) * First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2013) * [[Frances Pomeroy Naismith Award]] (2014) * [[American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] MVP ([[2014 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|2014]]) * No. 2 [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|retired by Louisville Cardinals]] * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2009) {{center|*''Later vacated''}} }} '''Russ Antoin Smith''' (born April 19, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for Pallacanestro Nardò of [[Serie A2 (basketball)|Serie A2]] in Italy. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]], playing a starring role as a junior in helping them win the 2013 NCAA championship, while earning third-team [[All-American]] by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] and the ''[[Sporting News]]''.{{cite web|url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032813aaa.html|title=Men's Basketball's Smith Earns NABC All-America Honors|publisher=GoCards.com|date=March 28, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215043152/http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032813aaa.html|archive-date=December 15, 2013}}{{cite web|title=Russ Smith named Sporting News All-American|url=http://www.whas11.com/sports/Russ-Smith-named-Sporting-News-All-American-197233781.html |work=WHAS11.com |date=March 11, 2013 |access-date=March 11, 2013 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006093419/http://www.whas11.com/sports/Russ-Smith-named-Sporting-News-All-American-197233781.html |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }} As a senior at Louisville, he was named a consensus first-team All-American. {{As of|2023|3|5|df=US}}, his 65-point performance remains the [[NBA G League]] single game scoring record. ==High school career== Smith was born in [[New York City]] at NY Presbyterian Hospital to Paulette A. O'Neal and Russell Smith. He went to [[Archbishop Molloy High School]] in Queens, N.Y. and played basketball for head coach [[Jack Curran]]. He led the New York City Catholic league ([[Catholic High School Athletic Association|CHSAA]]) in scoring as a junior averaging 24.5 points a game and as a senior averaging 29.6 points,{{cite web|last=Winn |first=Luke |title=11 Russdiculous facts about Louisville's Russ Smith |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20121221/russ-smith-louisville/ |work=SportsIllustrated.cnn.com |publisher=Sports Illustrated |date=December 21, 2012 |access-date=April 1, 2013 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140325190324/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20121221/russ-smith-louisville/ |archive-date=March 25, 2014 }} he also had a 7.3 rebound and 3.2 assist average his final season for the Molloy Stanners. His career high in points was 47, which he reached twice as a senior against St. Francis Prep and Christ the King. Smith was named to the 2009 New York State Sportswriters Association all-state team, made the first-team all-CHSAA "AA", and New York Daily News All-Queens first team as a senior. He played in the 2009 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] Regional Game at Madision Square Garden on April 18. Where he scored 27 points and earned co-MVP honors as his City team beat the Suburban team 129–120. Russ played prep school basketball at [[South Kent School]] in 2010 averaging 19.7 points and 3.9 assists a game as South Kent went 20–12 on the season.{{cite web|title=Russ Smith Bio|url=http://www.gocards.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=357|work=GoCards.com|publisher=Louisville Cardinals|access-date=March 31, 2013}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2010}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Russ Smith | position = G | hometown = Brooklyn, NY | highschool = Archbishop Molloy High School, NY
South Kent School, CT | feet = 6 | inches = 0 | weight = 165 | 40 = | commitdate = November 15, 2009 | scout stars = 2 | rivals stars = 3 | espn grade = 88 }} |} ==College career== ===Recruitment=== Louisville overlooked Smith at first. Assistant coaches [[Ralph Willard]] and [[Steve Masiello]] were on a recruiting trip in South Kent in September 2009, looking at another player. They saw Smith, who they thought would be perfect for their system. Masiello had also known Smith's father since he was 15. Louisville started looking at Smith seriously, and Smith liked Louisville so much that he tried to commit before he had a scholarship offer. ===Freshman year=== Upon coming to school, Smith chose uniform #2. Injuries limited Smith's playing time as a freshman. He had a broken foot, concussion, strained foot, and sore knee during the season and only saw action in 17 games. Smith was so miserable with the injuries and lack of playing time he decided to leave Louisville and go back home. But that day against West Virginia, coach Pitino put him in and told him to play hard. He had 3 points, 2 rebounds, one steal, and played good defense in his nine minutes of action.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310260097|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110129005612/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310260097|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 29, 2011|title=Peyton Siva's layup helps Louisville tip West Virginia|work=ESPN.com|date=January 26, 2011|access-date=April 9, 2013}} Helping spark the Cardinals' comeback from down 11 to win by 1, when [[Peyton Siva]] hit a layup at the buzzer. After that, he decided to stay. The Cardinals reached the championship game of the [[2011 Big East men's basketball tournament]] but lost to [[2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]].{{cite web|title=2011–12 Louisville Basketball Media Guide|url=http://www.guide.provations.com/louisville/2011mensbasketball#pg64|work=Player Bio: Peyton Siva|publisher=University of Louisville|access-date=January 29, 2012|archive-date=June 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120613210253/http://www.guide.provations.com/louisville/2011mensbasketball#pg64|url-status=dead}} Louisville finished the season 25–10, 12–6 in the [[2010–11 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2010–11 Big East season]] tied for 3rd in the conference. They received an at-large bid and a #4 seed in the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA tournament]] where they were upset in the second round by #13 seeded [[2010–11 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] 61–62.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310760097|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110319132555/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310760097|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 19, 2011|title=Demonte Harper's 3-pointer with seconds left lifts Morehead State past Louisville|work=ESPN.com|date=March 18, 2011|access-date=April 9, 2013}} ===Sophomore year=== During his sophomore year in [[2011-12 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2011–12]], Smith provided a spark off the bench. He was second in scoring despite being sixth in mins played for the Cardinals.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/97/year/2012/louisville-cardinals|title=Louisville Cardinals 2011–12 Statistics – Team and Player Stats – Men's College Basketball – ESPN|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 9, 2013}} In January 2012 he earned the nickname "Russdiculous" given to him by head coach [[Rick Pitino]], who has named a race horse "Russdiculous" also.{{cite web|first=Luke |last=Winn |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1206631/1/index.htm |title=Put Your Trust In ... Russ? |publisher=SportsIllustrated.cnn.com |date=December 24, 2012 |access-date=April 9, 2013 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130131050850/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1206631/1/index.htm |archive-date=January 31, 2013 }} Smith set a school record for steals in a season with 87 steals in his 39 games played. Louisville won four games in four nights to win the [[2012 Big East men's basketball tournament|2012 Big East tournament championship]]. The Cardinals advanced to the Final Four of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]], upsetting #1 seed [[2011–12 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 57–44 in the sweet sixteen and defeating #7 seed [[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the regional final, where Smith led Louisville with 19 points in the game.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320840097|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327060054/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320840097|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 27, 2012|title=Louisville ends game on 23-8 run to stun Florida, reach Final Four|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2012|access-date=April 9, 2013}} Before losing in the national semifinals to [[Kentucky–Louisville rivalry|arch-rival]] and eventual national champion [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. Smith averaged 11.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 2.2 steals a game for the Cardinals, who finished the season with a 30–10 record.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2531038/russ-smith |title=Russ Smith Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=ESPN.go.com|access-date=April 9, 2013}} ===Junior year=== [[File:Russ Smith Peyton Siva championship trophy.jpg|thumb|right|Smith (left) and [[Peyton Siva]] (right) with the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] trophy.]] Before the start of the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 basketball season]] the [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team]] was picked to finish 1st in the [[2012–13 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East Conference]] in polls done by Big East writers{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Waters|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/10/louisville_tops_big_east_write.html|title=Louisville tops Big East writers' poll; Cardinals dominate all-league teams|publisher=Syracuse.com|date=October 16, 2012|access-date=April 9, 2013}} and coaches.{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Jared|url=http://newyork.sbnation.com/2012/10/17/3517762/big-east-basketball-media-day-2012-coaches-poll-all-big-east-preseason|title=Big East basketball media day: Coaches' poll, All-Big East preseason teams and news|publisher=Newyork.sbnation.com|date=October 17, 2012|access-date=April 9, 2013}} Louisville finished the regular season with a 26–5 record and 14–4 in the Big East to tie for a share of the Big East regular season championship with [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] and [[2012–13 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]], who also finished with a 14–4 conference record.{{cite web|last=Ennis|first=Mark|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2013/3/12/4091940/2013-big-east-tournament-preview-louisville-georgetown-syracuse-otto-porter |title=2013 Big East tournament preview: Louisville and Georgetown favorites in league's swan song|publisher=SBNation.com|date=March 12, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} Smith learned about the death of his high school coach Jack Curran before the start of the [[2013 Big East men's basketball tournament|2013 Big East tournament]]. Louisville played [[2012–13 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in their first game of the tournament, Smith scored 28 points and said "Today was definitely Coach Curran Day for me, and it will be the rest of my life" in postgame interview that aired live on [[ESPN]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330730097|title=Russ Smith leads Louisville over Villanova, into Big East semifinals|work=ESPN.com |date=March 15, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} Russ was named to the Big East All-Tournament Team{{cite web|last=Mike|first=Waters|title=Louisville's Peyton Siva joins Georgetown's Patrick Ewing as the only two-time winners of the Big East Most Outstanding Player award|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/03/louisvilles_peyton_siva_joins.html|work=Syracuse.com|date=March 17, 2013 |publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard|access-date=March 17, 2013}} and his team won the Big East tournament Championship game versus [[2012-13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] by a score of 78–61 after trailing by 13 at halftime.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330750097|title=Louisville rallies from 16 down to win 2nd straight Big East title|work=ESPN.com|date=March 17, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} Louisville, with a 29–5 record, was selected the #1 overall seed for the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9063277/2013-ncaa-tournament-louisville-cardinals-named-top-overall-seed|title=Louisville claims top overall seed|work=ESPN.com|date=March 26, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} In his first two games of the NCAA tournament at [[Rupp Arena]] he had 23 points versus [[2012–13 North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball team|North Carolina A&T]] and had 27 against [[2012–13 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]]. Louisville fans liked what Smith was doing on the floor so much they started chanting RussArena{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330820097|title=Louisville routs Colorado State behind Russ Smith's 27 points|work=ESPN.com|date=March 23, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} near the end of the Colorado State game and made a Twitter hashtag #RussArena.{{cite web|first=Tommy|last=Tomlinson|url=http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/43306768/|title=Russ Smith could be the key to Louisville's Final Four run. | SportsonEarth.com : Tommy Tomlinson Article |publisher=SportsonEarth.com|date=March 26, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} He tied his career high of 31 points and the Cardinals beat the [[2012-13 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon Ducks]] 77–69 in the Sweet Sixteen.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330880097|title=Russ Smith scores 31 points to boost Louisville into Elite 8|work=ESPN.com|date=March 30, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} In Louisville's 85–63 regional final win against [[2012-13 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], Smith recorded 23 points and was subsequently named the Most Outstanding Player of the tournament's Midwest Region. During the Duke game Smith witnessed [[Kevin Ware]] suffer a horrible broken leg accident that left the team very emotional. Ware said "Just go win this game for me. Just go win this game. Don't worry about me, I'm fine." while being attended to by medical staff who was preparing him for a trip to the hospital. Louisville outscored Duke 64 to 43 after the Ware injury and credited Ware's positive attitude about his injury for their win.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330900097|title=Emotional Louisville overcomes injury to Kevin Ware to reach Final Four|publisher=ESPN.go.com|date=April 1, 2013|access-date=April 1, 2013}} In Louisville's next game Smith had 21 points in a 72–68 win over [[2012–13 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]] in the Final Four.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330960097|title=Louisville edges upstart Wichita State, advances to NCAA title game|publisher=ESPN.go.com|date=April 7, 2013|access-date=April 9, 2013}} Smith averaged 18.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 2.1 steals this season for the Cardinals who won the national championship over Michigan with a 35–5 record. The championship was later taken away for recruits receiving impermissible benefits.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/2531038/russ-smith |title=Russ Smith Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=ESPN.go.com |access-date=April 9, 2013 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140329072925/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/51478/russ-smith |archive-date=March 29, 2014 }} ===Senior year=== On April 24, 2013, Smith announced he would stay at Louisville for his senior year in an attempt to improve his draft stock the upcoming year.{{cite web|first=Morty|last=Ain|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9893546/louisville-guard-russ-smith-why-returning-senior-season-espn-magazine|title=The return of Russdiculous|work=ESPN.com|date=November 1, 2013|access-date=November 1, 2013}} On February 28, he was named one of the 10 semi-finalists for [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by AT&T |url=http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx |work=Naismith Awards |access-date=February 18, 2014 |date=February 28, 2014 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006124015/http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }} Louisville finished the season with a 31–6 record, earning a 4 seed in the tournament. Louisville opened against [[2013–14 Manhattan Jaspers basketball team|Manhattan]] in the second round, Smith led the game in scoring with 18 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400546903|title=Louisville comes alive late to squeak past Manhattan|work=ESPN.com|date=March 21, 2014|access-date=March 21, 2014}} After Manhattan, Louisville advanced 66–51 against [[2013–14 Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball team|Saint Louis]]. Smith tallied up 11 points and tied for the most assists with 7.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400548508|title=Louisville tops Saint Louis, reaches Sweet 16 for 3rd straight year|work=ESPN.com|date=March 22, 2014|access-date=March 22, 2014}} Smith ended his college career with 23 points in the Sweet Sixteen, losing against Kentucky.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400548877|title=Kentucky uses late surge to boot defending champ Louisville|work=ESPN.com|date=March 29, 2014|access-date=March 29, web|first=Jonathan|last=Lintner|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2014/03/31/russ-smith-makes-ap-american-team/7117111/|title=Russ Smith makes two All-America teams|publisher=Courier-Journal.com|date=March 31, 2014|access-date=March 31, 2014}} On January 22, 2022, his No. 2 jersey was retired by the Cardinals.{{Cite web|title=Russ Smith all smiles as Louisville makes him fifth Cardinals men's basketball player to have jersey retired|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33125774/russ-smith-all-smiles-louisville-makes-fifth-cardinals-men-basketball-player-jersey-retired|access-date=January 23, revealed|work=ESPN.com|date=May 31, 2014|access-date=May 31, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===New Orleans Pelicans (2014–2015)=== On June 26, 2014, Smith was selected with the 47th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Polacek|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2067869-russ-smith-drafted-by-76ers-latest-news-reaction-and-analysis|title=Russ Smith Drafted by 76ers: Latest News, Reaction and Analysis|work=BleacherReport.com|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=June 26, 2014}} The next day, his rights were traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for the rights to [[Pierre Jackson]].{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140627-pierre-jackson|title=Sixers Acquire Rights To Point Guard Pierre Jackson|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2014|access-date=June 28, 2014}} Following the draft, Smith noted his frustration in some draft analysts questioning his efficiency. He was frustrated by teams waffling over his ability to play point guard at the NBA level, and was frustrated that several unnamed big-time NBA draft prospects avoided workouts with him in the two-month build-up to the draft.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Greer|title=Russ Smith frustrated by NBA draft, ready to start|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2014/06/26/louisvilles-russ-smith-selected-xxx-xx-pick-nba-draft/11411759/|work=Courier-Journal.com|date=January 7, 2015|access-date=February 8, 2016}} He later signed his rookie scale contract with the Pelicans on July 15.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-russ-smith|title=Pelicans Sign Russ Smith|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2014}} During his rookie season with the Pelicans, he had multiple assignments with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|access-date=December 17, 2015|work=NBA.com|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2015)=== On January 12, 2015, Smith was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three-team deal involving the Pelicans and the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-green-smith-three-team-trade-150112|title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Jeff Green and Russ Smith in three-team trade with Boston Celtics and New Orleans Pelicans|work=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2015|access-date=January 12, 2015}} He was assigned multiple times to the [[Iowa Energy]] in his rookie season. Smith made his playoff debut on May 3, 2015, in a 101–86 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the Western Conference semi-finals.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150503/MEMGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Warriors roll past Grizzlies 101-86 in Game 1 of West semis|work=NBA.com|date=May 3, 2015|access-date=May 3, 2015}} On December 17, 2015, Smith was reassigned to the Iowa Energy,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-assign-ennis-martin-smith-iowa-energy-151217|title=Grizzlies assign James Ennis, Jarrell Martin and Russ Smith to Iowa Energy|work=NBA.com|date=December 17, 2015|access-date=December 17, 2015}} but was recalled later that day.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5081258|title=Memphis Grizzlies Recall James Ennis, Jarell Martin and Russ Smith from Iowa Energy|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 17, 2015|access-date=December 17, 2015}} He was reassigned again on December 22,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/ennis-martin-smith-to-iowa-151222|title=Grizzlies re-assign James Ennis, Jarell Martin and Russ Smith to Iowa Energy|work=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2015|access-date=December 22, 2015}} and recalled two days later.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5083117|title=Memphis Grizzlies Recall James Ennis, Jarell Martin and Russ Smith from the Iowa Energy|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 24, 2015|access-date=December 24, 2015}} On December 29, he was waived by the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizz-sign-hollins-151229|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign center Ryan Hollins|date=December 29, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 29, 2015}} ===Delaware 87ers (2016)=== On January 13, 2016, Smith was acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/delaware-87ers-acquire-russ-smith/|title=Delaware 87ers acquire Russ Smith|date=January 13, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160118193032/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/delaware-87ers-acquire-russ-smith/|archive-date=January 18, 2016|url-status=dead}} Two days later, he made his debut for the 87ers in a 119–104 win over [[Raptors 905]], scoring a team-high 37 points in 28 minutes of action off the bench.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160115/RAPDEL/|title=87ers Run Past Raptors|date=January 15, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 16, 2016|archive-date=January 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116153437/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160115/RAPDEL/|url-status=dead}} On February 1, 2016, he was named NBA D-League Performer of the Week for games played Monday, January 25 through Sunday, January 31. The honor was the first of Smith's career. He helped Delaware to a 2–1 week, averaging 28.7 points (fifth in the league) on 48 percent shooting (28-for-58) to go with a league-leading 8.7 assists, 4.3 rebounds and 2.0 steals.{{cite web|title=87ers Guard Russ Smith Named NBA Development League Performer of the Week|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/russ-smith-nba-development-league-performer-of-week-020116/|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2016|access-date=February 8, 2016}} On March 18, he recorded his first career triple-double after recording 20 points, 13 rebounds and 16 assists in a 116–98 win over the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021500392/|title=Fort Wayne Mad Ants 98 - Delaware 87ers 116|publisher=G-League Stats|date=March 18, 2016|access-date=April 15, 2020}} On March 23, he set a D-League scoring record with 65 points on 24-of-42 shooting from the field in a 140–129 loss to the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite web|title=Russdiculous! Top Prospect Russ Smith Pours in Record 65 Points for Delaware 87ers|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160323/delctn/|work=NBA.com|date=March 23, 2016|access-date=March 24, 2016}}{{cite web|title=Russ Smith Goes Off for NBA D-League Record 65 Points!|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3f39wzZBGaE|work=YouTube.com|date=March 23, 2016|access-date=March 25, 2016}} {{As of|2022|3|3|df=US}}, the record still stood as did his record of 105 points in consecutive games.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/breaking-down-nik-stauskas-wild-57-point-performance|title=Breaking Down Nik Stauskas' Wild Two-Game Stretch|accessdate=May 7, 2022|date=March 3, 2022|work=[[NBA.com]]}} On March 29, he was waived by the 87ers after being deemed to have a season-ending injury.{{cite web|title=NBA D-League Transactions |url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 31, 2016 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401043327/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=April 1, 2016 }} ===Europe (2016)=== On July 27, 2016, Smith signed a one-year contract with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray Odeabank]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish BSL]] and [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/207799/galatasaray-signs-russ-smith.html|title= Galatasaray signs Russ Smith|date=July 27, 2016|access-date=July 27, 2016|publisher=Sportando.com}} In December 2016, he parted ways with Galatasaray.{{cite news|title=Galatasaray parted ways with Russ Smith|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/featured/365740/galatasaray-parted-ways-russ-smith|access-date=January 10, 2017|work=Eurohoops.net|date=December 17, 2016}} ===Return to the Delaware 87ers (2017)=== On January 20, 2017, Smith was re-acquired by the Delaware 87ers.{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/Sevens/status/822543651817607172|title=x.com}} ===China (2017–2021)=== On June 3, 2017, Smith signed with Luoyang Zhonghe of China for the 2017 [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]] season.{{cite news|title=Russ Smith signs in China with Luoyang where he averaged 60 points per game which is a world record.|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/236057/russ-smith-signs-in-china-with-luoyang.html|access-date=July 5, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=June 3, 2017}} In his debut with Luoyang, Smith scored 62 points (including seven 3-pointers made) and recorded three steals in a 138–123 loss to the Anhui Lightning.{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2017/0625_15107_21474.asp|title=Anhui 138 - Luoyang 123|publisher=EuroBasket|date=June 25, 2017|access-date=April 15, 2020}} On July 5, 2017, Smith scored a career-high 81 points to go along with eight rebounds and seven assists in a 142–130 win over the Henan Golden Elephants.{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2017/0705_21474_9956.asp|title=Luoyang 142 - Henan 130|publisher=EuroBasket|date=July 5, 2017|access-date=April 15, 2020}} Russ Smith averaged 61.2 points per game that season & applied for a world record. After that summer league's campaign wrapped up, he signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] for the 2017-18 [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] season.{{cite web |title=Fujian Sturgeons sign Andrew Nicholson and Russ Smith |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/china/285361/fujian-sturgeons-sign-andrew-nicholson-and-russ-smith.html |website=Sportando |access-date=August 13, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{Cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/2018/03/26/russ-smith-on-possible-nba-comeback-ascent-at-louisville-reaction-to-vacated-title-61-2-ppg-average-in-china-and-more/|title = Russ Smith on possible NBA comeback, ascent at Louisville, reaction to vacated title, 61.2 PPG average in China and more|date = March 26, 2018}} ===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2021–2022)=== On December 30, 2021, Smith was acquired and activated by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=December 30, 2021|access-date=December 30, 2021}} On January 7, 2022, in his first game in the G League since 2017, Smith scored 43 points in a 94–103 loss to the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web |last1=Rutherford |first1=Mike |title=Russ Smith explodes for 43 points in G League return |url=https://www.cardchronicle.com/2022/1/7/22872016/russ-smith-explodes-for-43-points-in-g-league-return |website=Card Chronicle |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=January 8, 2022 |date=January 7, 2022}} On January 31, he suffered a season-ending shoulder injury. Smith averaged 16.4 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game.{{cite news |title=Russ Smith: Suffers season-ending injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/russ-smith-suffers-season-ending-injury/ |access-date=February 13, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 31, 2022}} ===Hapoel Be'er Sheva (2022)=== On September 2, 2022, he signed with [[Hapoel Be'er Sheva B.C.|Hapoel Be'er Sheva]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-beer-sheva-signs-russ-smith-to-replace-desonta-bradford/|title=Hapoel Beer Sheva signs Russ Smith to replace Desonta Bradford|date=September 2, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 2, 2022|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} ===Tabiat Eslamshahr (2024–2025)=== On November 18, 2024, Smith signed with Tabiat Eslamshahr of [[Iranian Basketball Super League]].{{cite web |title=Russ Smith signs at Tabiat |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Iran/news/902541/Russ-Smith-signs-at-Tabiat |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=November 23, 2024 |date=November 18, 2024}} ===Pallacanestro Nardò (2025–present)=== On February 6, 2025, Smith signed with Pallacanestro Nardò of [[Serie A2 (basketball)|Serie A2]] in Italy.{{cite web |title=ECCO L'UOMO DEI SOGNI, RUSS SMITH TORNA A "CASA" |url=https://www.nardobasket.it/news/259423374854/ecco-l-uomo-dei-sogni-russ-smith-torna-a-casa |website=Nardò Basket |access-date=February 7, 2025 |date=February 6, 2025}} ==The Basketball Tournament== Smith joined other Louisville basketball alumni for the 2023 and 2024 [[The Basketball Tournament]] aka TBT. He led ''The Ville'' team in scoring for the '23 season, losing in the regional championship.{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/russ-smith-2024-tbt|title=Russ Smith to Rejoin Louisville Alumni TBT Team|first=Matthew|last=McGavic|date=March 19, 2024|magazine=Sports Illustrated}} He led the team in scoring again for the '24 season, and lost to the [[Kentucky basketball]] alumni's team ''La Familia'' in the quarterfinals'.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/2024-tbt-game-4|title=The Ville Falls to La Familia in TBT
